questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

The table shows the marginal costs of production and marginal benefits of consumption. marginal private marginal social marginal private marginal social cost ($) cost ($) benefit ($) benefit ($) 100 150 150 200 What is demonstrated in these values?

options.A: a negative consumption externality
options.C: Pareto optimality

questions.questionText: A cost-benefit analysis concludes that a nuclear power station project might be socially worthwhile, although it will take 10 years to bring into operation. Why might a government decide not to undertake the project?

options.A: Cost-benefit analysis has no method for valuing the long-term impact of a project.
options.B: Cost-benefit analysis is only suitable for private sector projects.
options.C: The government believes that the project has too high an opportunity cost.
options.D: The government’s policy is to restrict the extent of the market system.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows a budget line indicating combinations of good Y and good X that a consumer could buy with a given income. The combinations shown by points S and T both lie on the same normal indifference curve. good Y Z S W T O good X Which statement is logically correct?

options.A: The consumer is indifferent between combinations W, S and T.
options.B: The consumer prefers combination T to combination W.
options.C: The consumer prefers combination W to combination S.
options.D: The consumer prefers combination Z to combination T.

questions.questionText: The table shows some of the assumptions of perfect competition and monopolistic competition. Which pairing is correct? perfect competition monopolistic competition

options.A: identical products freedom of entry and exit
options.C: large number of firms small number of firms

questions.questionText: What is a feature of a natural monopoly?

options.A: The monopoly produces a product that has no close substitutes.
options.B: Average costs fall over the entire range of output.
options.C: The monopoly controls the supply of its raw materials.
options.D: Diseconomies of scale set in at low levels of output.

questions.questionText: A firm is already the monopoly producer of product X. Which strategy might the firm pursue in order to prevent new firms from entering the market for product X?

options.A: co-operation
options.C: predatory pricing

questions.questionText: What makes collusion between firms in an oligopolistic industry more difficult?

options.A: barriers to the entry of new firms
options.B: limited scope for cost reduction via innovation
options.C: significant product differentiation between firms
options.D: stability in the market demand for the product

questions.questionText: What is the defining characteristic of an oligopolistic industry?

options.A: contestability
options.C: mutual interdependence

questions.questionText: A perfectly competitive firm is currently producing at a level of output where its marginal cost is above both its average total cost and the market price. What would be the effect on price and output if the firm were to maximise its profit? effect on output effect on price

options.A: decrease increase
options.C: increase decrease

questions.questionText: In which industrial sector is a small firm most likely to survive?

options.A: banking
options.C: insurance

questions.questionText: A firm wishes to avoid attracting competition from new entrants. It charges the maximum price that is consistent with this aim. In which type of market does this firm operate?

options.A: a contestable market
options.C: a monopsonistic market

questions.questionText: In which market structure will the industry price be unaffected by a change in the output of one individual firm?

options.A: monopolistic competition
options.C: oligopoly

questions.questionText: In 2015 the price of oil fell dramatically. As a result, 65000 jobs were lost in the North Sea oil industry. How would this be represented on a diagram for the labour market for oil workers?

options.A: a movement down the marginal revenue product curve
options.B: a shift towards the horizontal axis of the marginal cost curve
options.C: a shift towards the origin of the marginal revenue product curve
options.D: a shift towards the vertical axis of the average cost curve

questions.questionText: An actor is paid $100000 a year. The next best paid job he could get is as a lecturer at $60000 a year. What are his transfer earnings and his economic rent? transfer earnings economic rent
What is not an outcome of the existence of private property rights?

options.A: They encourage private owners to conserve property when its value is expected to rise.
options.B: They give private owners the incentive to manage their property carefully.
options.C: They make a private owner accountable for damage to others from property misuse.
options.D: They prevent private owners gaining from using resources to benefit others.

questions.questionText: A state-owned concern is privatised as a monopoly. What would increase the likelihood of its achieving productive efficiency?

options.A: an absence of barriers to entry
options.B: the need for capital representing a high sunk cost
options.C: the existence of significant economies of scale
options.D: variable costs forming a small proportion of total cost

questions.questionText: Which policy is most likely to both increase productivity and improve equity?

options.A: a switch in taxation from income to expenditure
options.B: the introduction of minimum prices on essential foodstuffs
options.C: the privatisation of state-run transport systems
options.D: the supply of free health care

questions.questionText: Which indicator is least likely to be used when measuring the comparative economic development of a country?

options.A: adult literacy rate
options.C: level of real GNP per head

questions.questionText: What needs to be removed to improve nominal GDP as a measure of comparative living standards?

options.A: the effects of exports and imports
options.B: the effects of exports and population change
options.C: the effects of population change and imports
options.D: the effects of population change and inflation

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the age structure of the Polish population in 2015 and the predicted structure in 2050. Since 2013, the retirement age in Poland has been 67 for men and 65 for women. 2015 (%) 2050 (%)

The table gives information on differences between females and males in 2013 in the Human Development Index and Gross National Income per capita in countries with different levels of development. GNI per capita HDI (US $ purchasing power parity 2011) female male female male very high development .871 .887 26667 53681 high development .710 .733 9426 16966 medium development .565 .622 3199 8619 low development .446 .506 2011 3789 What can be concluded from the table?

options.A: Females are closer to males in earning ability than in development opportunities.
options.B: Females are closest to males in development opportunities in countries with low development.

options.A: JK B JL C NY F

questions.questionText: In the Quantity Theory of Money equation, MV = PT, V is defined as the income velocity of circulation. Which change would tend to reduce the value of V?

options.A: a move to monthly rather than weekly salary payments by firms
options.C: an increase in the use of cash machines to reduce money balances held
options.D: an increase in the use of credit cards by individuals

questions.questionText: What moves from households to firms within the circular flow of income?

options.A: factor services
options.C: savings

questions.questionText: What is meant by liquidity preference?

options.A: a desire to be paid in cash rather than by cheque
options.B: a desire to be paid monthly rather than weekly
options.C: a desire to hold assets that are convertible into cash
options.D: a desire to hold money rather than other assets

questions.questionText: What is an appropriate government policy for closing a deflationary gap?

options.A: an increase in the rate of interest
options.B: an open market sale of bonds
options.C: an increase in government spending

questions.questionText: Which policy is most likely to contribute to people ending up in a poverty trap?

options.A: legal minimum wage
options.C: prevention of cheaper imports

questions.questionText: During year 1, a government announces a temporary one-year reduction in the level of indirect taxation balanced by an equivalent temporary one-year increase in direct taxation. What is most likely to be the impact on household saving in year 1 and in year 2? impact on household impact on household saving in year 1 saving in year 2

options.A: decrease decrease
options.C: increase decrease
